insurer: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified (varies by plan; e.g., Optima Secure: 5/10/15/20/25/50/100/200 Lakhs as per Annexure C)

great.name: Room Rent
great.quote: Room rent limit shall be At Actuals unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule.
great.explanation: Room rent is payable at actuals unless a different limit is mentioned in the Policy Schedule. This reduces the risk of room-rent linked deductions and gives flexibility to choose a room.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: The Secure Benefit will be applicable only after exhaustion of Base Sum Insured.
great.explanation: Secure Benefit becomes available only after the Base Sum Insured is fully used up. This provides extra insurer-funded coverage for large or multiple claims.

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: The restored Sum Insured can be used even for the same illness for which an admissible claim has been paid during the Policy Year and also for any other Illness covered under the Policy.
great.explanation: Restored Sum Insured can be used again in the same policy year even for the same illness. This is stronger than restores that work only for unrelated illnesses.

great.name: NCB
great.quote: This Cover will be applied irrespective of number of claims made under the expiring Policy.
great.explanation: Plus Benefit applies on renewal irrespective of the number of claims in the expiring policy. This means your extra cover does not get wiped out just because you claimed.

great.name: Co-pay
great.quote: Def. 8. Co-Payment means a cost sharing requirement under a health insurance policy that provides that the policyholder/insured will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claims amount.
great.explanation: Only a definition of co-payment is provided and no applied co-pay is stated here. No co-pay is charged on this plan based on this wording, so the insurer pays 100% of admissible claims.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing disease (PED)... shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months (Unless specified otherwise in the Policy Schedule) of continuous coverage...
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are not covered for the first 36 months unless the Policy Schedule specifies otherwise. This is a common market waiting period and affects claims for existing conditions.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage...
good.reference: Section C.1(b)(i) 	6 Specified Disease/Procedure waiting period (Page 28-29)
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are covered only after 24 months of continuous coverage. This delays eligibility for those conditions even if they are not pre-existing.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident...
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered in the first 30 days from the first policy start date, except for accidents. This is standard and mainly impacts early claims soon after purchase.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Such expenses shall be indemnified if the same were incurred upto 60 days unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule, immediately prior to the date of admission.
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days before hospitalization are covered, unless the Policy Schedule states otherwise. This helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Such expenses shall be indemnified if the same were incurred upto 180 days unless otherwise specified in the Policy Schedule, immediately post the date of discharge from the Hospital.
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 180 days after discharge are covered, unless the Policy Schedule states otherwise. This supports follow-up treatment and medicines during recovery.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: The Company shall indemnify expenses incurred... towards Ambulance transportation in an airplane or helicopter for Emergency Care...
good.explanation: Emergency air ambulance (airplane/helicopter) expenses are covered when this optional benefit is in force. This can be valuable for critical transfers but is not part of the default cover.

good.name: Consumables
good.quote: The Company shall indemnify the Insured Person for the Non-Medical Expenses listed under Annexure B to this Policy incurred in relation to a claim admissible under Section B -1 (Base Coverage)...
good.explanation: Non-medical/consumable expenses listed in Annexure B are payable only if the optional Protect Benefit is opted. Choosing it can reduce out-of-pocket spend on items typically excluded.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Non-Medical expenses such as... Full list of Non -Medical Expenses is attached as ANNEXURE B... (Annexure B includes items such as) "GLOVES" ... "MASK" ... "NEBULISATION KIT" ...
bad.reference: Section C.3(k) 	6 Specific Exclusions (Page 32) + Annexure B (Pages 49-50)
bad.explanation: Consumables/non-medical items listed in Annexure B (e.g., gloves, masks, nebulisation kit) are excluded under the base policy. This can materially increase your hospital bill unless you have the optional Protect Benefit.
